items.summary: RIL's consolidated revenue rose 27. 8% year-on-year to ₹3. 6 lakh crore in the September quarter, with Ebitda of ₹62,409 crore at a record high but up only 23. 9%. The O2C business led growth, pushing Ebitda 67. 9% to ₹25,203 crore and nearly 40% of group total. Retail Ebitda fell 10. 2% to ₹6,120 crore amid margin pressure from digital commerce investments and input costs. Jio Platforms reported double-digit revenue and profit growth after its October listing, with customer base rising 7. 1% to 542. 4 million and 5G users reaching 55. 3%.
items.title: Reliance eyes growth from O2C, retail and Jio businesses

items.summary: Asian share markets fell Monday amid fears over the sustainability of the AI investment boom and high oil prices limiting bond appeal. Concerns about corporate default insurance costs rose, while gold hit a one-year low. The week's focus is on earnings from Apple, AMD and Palantir after Intel dropped nearly 29 per cent Friday. Goldman Sachs analysts expect hyperscaler capex to reach $800 billion this year, with S&P 500 EPS growth of about 30 per cent in 2026.
items.title: Asian shares slip as AI spending worries weigh on tech ahead of Apple earnings

items.summary: Hong Kong is considering new rules targeting asset-intensive reinsurance, one of the fastest-growing segments of its insurance market, according to people familiar with the matter. The Hong Kong Insurance Authority has sought industry feedback on changes that would require insurers to either notify or seek approval depending on circumstances such as credit ratings and materiality. A revised guideline is expected to take effect in 2027, the regulator said. Representatives for several firms declined to comment.
items.title: Hong Kong Considers Rules for Asset-Intensive Reinsurance

items.summary: Kranthi Bathini of WealthMills Securities said festive activity extending into November, stronger corporate earnings and renewed foreign buying could support Indian equities. He noted October gains in the Sensex (1.9%) and Nifty (2.7%), while mid- and small-cap indices fell 4% and 6.3%. Global uncertainties and high oil prices remain key risks. Aditya Agarwala of InvestValue Capital advised favouring companies with strong domestic earnings visibility and pricing power.
items.title: Indian equity strategist sees November tailwinds amid macro risks

items.summary: The Supreme Court upheld a Delhi High Court order permitting the Income Tax Department to reassess Chetan and Nitin Sabharwal, sons of former Chief Justice YK Sabharwal. The bench affirmed that a March 31, 2015 notice under Section 148 was validly issued for assessment years 2008-09 and 2009-10 regarding share sale deals worth Rs 255 crore.
items.title: Supreme Court Upholds Tax Reassessment of Ex-CJI's Sons' Share Sales

items.summary:
The Ukrainian Air Force says its air raid alert app was hacked on Sunday and briefly warned Kyiv of a radiation threat. The Ukrainian Central Intelligence Agency said it was an app failure, while Russian authorities later blamed the hack. A partisan group called Atesh reportedly claimed responsibility for fake nuclear warnings inside Russia. Officials urged people to rely on official sources as false alerts spread nationwide before all-clear messages followed.

visual null},
items.title: Ukraine's Air Force Says Its Raid App Was Hacked With False Threats

items.summary: Binance customers withdrew a net $3.64bn (£2.72bn) of assets after the exchange reopened on Sunday following what is called the largest hack in history, which impacted $6.3bn worth of digital assets. The FBI and other organisations have accused North Korea's Lazarus Group (aka TraderTraitor) of responsibility. Binance says it has covered around 95% of stolen assets using treasury, futures insurance and emergency reserve funds, while reserving more than $6.34bn for the fallout; remaining recovery may take longer.
items.title: Binance Reopens After Record Hack as Customers Withdraw $3.6bn

items.summary: Donald Trump attacked Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed at an Iowa campaign event, repeatedly calling him a “jihadist” and saying Congress would need a special metal detector if he won. The comments targeted a tight Michigan race ahead of Tuesday’s midterms. El-Sayed responded to his ally Hayley Stevens after she endorsed Republican Mike Rogers.
items.title: Trump Attacks El-Sayed at Iowa Rally

items.summary: The administration of Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi is considering a registration system for foreign agents as part of planned antiespionage legislation. Under the expected rules, individuals and organizations collecting information or running influence operations on behalf of foreign governments would be required to register so their activities become visible. The government plans to submit related legislation to the Diet as early as next spring after an expert panel presented a concrete plan last week.
items.title: Japan Weighs Foreign Agent Registration in Antiespionage Law

items.summary: Ukraine's air force said on Sunday it suspected the country's nationwide Air Alarm application had probably been subjected to hostile interference, warning that threat notifications no longer reflected reality. The announcement came minutes after a local Kherson ceasefire ended and followed warnings from Ukraine's Centre for Countering Disinformation about mismatched information.
items.title: Ukraine's air force says nationwide alert app likely hacked after ceasefire ends

items.summary: Mass demonstrations in Germany that passed largely peacefully on Saturday erupted in violence at nightfall, with rioters facing off against police across Frankfurt, Cologne, Hamburg and Berlin. Authorities blocked Die Zeil in Frankfurt after demonstrators smashed shop windows and stole goods, arresting more than 30 people. Officers also arrested one person suspected of breaking into a gun store.
items.title: German Protests Turn Violent as Activists Clash with Police

items.summary: Supermodel Heidi Klum wore a gruesome severed-hand costume at her annual New York Halloween party on Oct 31, marking the event's 25th year. Only her eyes and mouth showed as blood dripped from her tongue. She said it took about five to six hours to get into the costume but making it took longer.
items.title: Heidi Klum Reveals Giant Hand Halloween Costume

items.summary: Finshots asks whether China's AI boom has already collapsed while the US still bets on it. It reports that over four months China's STAR 50 index fell 40%, wiping out nearly $480 billion in investor wealth, and describes how state-backed money drove retail traders into a speculative frenzy where AI stocks reached 42% of market value and 57% of trading volume. The piece frames the crash as part of a global reset, noting Nvidia shed $600 billion in one day after DeepSeek's low-cost model, while Alphabet lost nearly $500 billion this week. It draws an analogy to dark fibre from the dot-com era but cautions that AI chips may lose value faster than cables did, leaving companies still needing to make trillions pay off.
items.title: China's AI bubble bursts first as stocks crash

items.summary: A Learjet crashed into a South Florida neighborhood, killing nine people aboard the aircraft bound from Austin to the Bahamas. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said it came down near Cresthaven at 12:50 pm. The crash occurred less than seven miles from Mar-a-Lago and triggered a large fireball. FAA officials are sending a team to support an NTSB investigation, which is planned for Monday.
items.title: Learjet Crash Kills Nine Near Mar-a-Lago in Florida

items.summary: Delhi-NCR recorded an air quality index of 244 on October 21, the worst in 100 days, marking the start of a worsening pollution season. Gufran Beig and Prarthana Borah explain that El Niño could enhance weather trapping by reducing wind speeds further and weakening western disturbances, keeping pollutants suspended longer. CEEW's study found higher very poor and severe AQI days during an El Niño year (2023-’24) versus La Nina years. Experts caution that more long-term research is needed to isolate meteorological impacts from pollution sources, urging proactive mitigation of vehicular, industrial and crop-residue emissions.
items.title: El Niño May Intensify Delhi Winter Pollution Haze

items.summary: The Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) welcomed the GST Council's reforms, which remove arrest powers and raise the prosecution threshold fivefold from Rs 1 crore to Rs 5 crore. CII Director General Chandrajit Banerjee called it a landmark move toward trust-based governance that keeps penalties for serious violations while improving enforcement precision and reducing business uncertainty.
items.title: CII Praises GST Council Decriminalisation Reforms as Trust-Based Shift

items.summary: Zee Entertainment Enterprises Ltd clarified that an Enforcement Case Information Report (ECIR) registered against founder Subhash Chandra in his personal capacity carries no bearing on the company. The probe, led by the Central Bureau of Investigation after a first information report from LIC Housing Finance Ltd, alleges fraud causing public sector loss exceeding ₹1,322 crore over two credit facilities totaling ₹980 crore sanctioned in 2018.
items.title: Zee Separates Founder Probe From Corporate Operations

items.summary: Democratic party leaders failed to prevent a schism in Michigan's must-win Senate race, where Rep. Haley Stevens surprised colleagues by endorsing Republican nominee Mike Rogers after previously vowing to back Abdul El-Sayed. The defection drew praise from President Trump and calls for her removal from the House Democratic Caucus. Raskin called himself 'dumbfounded,' while Schumer labeled it a 'despicable betrayal.' Analysts see deep divides over Israel and party-left relations, with tensions likely extending into 2028.
items.title: Michigan Democrats Fracture Over Stevens' Rogers Endorsement

items.summary: Oilprice.com reports that samarium sells for as much as 346 times more in North America than in China, framing the gap as a preview of prices if Beijing curtails exports. The piece centers on REalloys (NASDAQ: ALOY), which it says is positioning to profit from one of the most serious shortages developing in America's rare earth supply chain. It notes that jet engines, EVs and wind turbines depend on magnets made with these metals, yet U.S. manufacturers still buy at Chinese prices; American firms purchase about 48,000 tonnes of magnet feedstock yearly while domestic output reached just 300 tonnes in 2025. The article attributes a metallization blind spot to Canaccord Genuity and cites REalloys' own claims that it holds the only operating heavy rare earth metallization capability in North America and reported $122.4 million in cash at end of June, with expansions fully funded. It flags an ownership conflict: Oilprice.com's owner holds shares or options in REalloys. The piece also surveys copper and lithium producers expanding into critical minerals but does not independently verify any company statement.
items.title: REalloys Bets on Rare-Earth Metallization Shortage

items.summary: Some investors are lowering expectations for US economic growth as red flags emerged over the sustainability of the country's rapid AI buildout. The tech-heavy Nasdaq slid into correction territory on Friday after investors unwound their AI bets, with Intel stock plunging 29% and S&P Global revising Meta's outlook to 'negative.' A strategist told Bloomberg that earnings misses are raising sober questions about AI investments.
items.title: Investors Trim US Growth Expectations After Weak AI Earnings

items.summary: AI-related fears over corporate cash flow and spending scale pushed default-insurance costs higher last week, while gold fell to a one-year low amid margin-call selling. Asian equities edged lower: the Nikkei dropped 0.5%, South Korea's index lost 0.8% after shedding 16% in October, and MSCI's Asia-Pacific outside Japan index eased 0.4%. The week's focus shifts to earnings from Apple, AMD and Palantir following Intel's near-29% fall. Futures imply a 72% chance of a quarter-point Fed rate rise, with only 55 basis points of tightening priced in versus more than 70 last month.
items.title: Asian shares slip as AI capex worries and Apple earnings loom

items.summary: Five of China's largest state-owned banks reported their fastest quarterly profit growth since 2021 or 2022, with gains between 6% and 11%, driven by stabilising net interest margins and steadier asset quality despite a slowing economy. Industrial and Commercial Bank of China posted 10% year-on-year net profit growth in the third quarter, while Agricultural Bank of China, China Construction Bank and Bank of Communications reported rates of 10.8%, 9.8% and 10.1%. Bank of China grew more slowly at 6.4% amid trade tensions. Analysts note that benefits from deposit repricing are fading but monetary easing supports margins, while rising bond gains add volatility as banks expand into chip sector investments.
items.title: China's Big Banks Report Fastest Quarterly Profit Growth in Years

items.summary: Ritesh Jain of Pinetree Macro says large-cap banks and IT stocks are seen as an anti-AI trade, drawing model-driven rather than broad foreign inflows. He notes a shift in global investment flows amid signs of deflation in the AI trade. BlackRock remains strategically overweight India, closely watching recent inflow pace after earlier outflows.
items.title: Foreign investors return to Indian markets as AI-trade optimism shifts global flows

items.summary: On Sunday, Sikh riot survivors and organisations questioned Congress's decision to hold the INDIA bloc rally on Nov 1, marking the 42nd anniversary of the 1984 anti-Sikh killings. The protest drew BJP leaders who saw political opportunity ahead of Punjab assembly elections due in 2027, framing the timing as ammunition against Congress.
items.title: Sikh Groups Question Timing of INDIA Bloc Rally on Massacre Anniversary

items.summary: Authorities said four US citizens and one each from Canada, Japan, Argentina, Mexico, Tunisia and the Czech Republic were among the 69 killed last week in a high-speed collision outside Urda. A legal body of police and forensics experts announced on Sunday the 10 latest confirmed foreign victims; all but three are now identified, with three missing-person reports still active for two Australians and one Japanese citizen.
items.title: Foreign nationals among dead in Spain train crash

items.summary: Democratic candidates lead in polls ahead of Tuesday's US midterm elections, with the party projected to clear 218 seats needed to flip the House and tie or edge key Senate races. The article notes recent polling misses—Trump outperforming predictions in 2016 and 2024, a Michigan primary that swung from predicted double-digit margins to just 1%, and Wisconsin's governor race flipping by less than a percent—to question accuracy. Clifford Young of Ipsos Public Affairs attributes challenges to declining landline reach and lower participation among conservatives. He cautions against overreading the data, noting polls can err both ways and that historical midterm patterns often favor the party out of power.
items.title: Polls Favor Democrats in Midterms Despite Past Polling Misses

items.summary: A submission to Victoria's construction royal commission, first reported by The Age, alleges the state government inflated costs and threatened a senior public servant into supporting its preferred Airport Rail Link route through Sunshine. An anonymous former planning expert reportedly said between $3.8 billion and $4.6 billion of unnecessary tunnelling was added to an alternate Maribyrnong route to make it less attractive than the Sunshine option, which totals up to $4.6 billion in additions. The government declined to comment, saying it would let the royal commission finish its work. Shadow Minister Evan Mulholland called the conduct bullying and intimidation, while minister Jaclyn Symes questioned the claims' sources. Centre for Public Integrity's William Partlett said the allegations may signal more to come.
items.title: Victorian Labor Alleged of Pressuring Officials Over Rail Route

items.summary: The Tasmanian Electoral Commission has finalised the Hobart City Council count, resulting in two women being elected to the body. Ben Lohberger had been expected to take up the deputy lord mayor position but failed to win a councillor seat. Under the rules, the deputy lord mayor will instead be chosen by councillors at their first meeting.
items.title: Hobart council gains two women as deputy mayor-elect loses seat

items.summary: Nine people aboard a Learjet traveling from Austin, Texas, to the Bahamas were killed when it crashed near Cresthaven and Greenacres in Palm Beach County on Sunday. The jet entered a steep dive after pilots reported turbulence and requested a climb. About 600 residents are being assisted with temporary shelter, according to the sheriff's office.
items.title: Learjet Crash Kills Nine in Florida Neighborhood

items.summary: A private Learjet 60 crashed into a South Florida neighborhood Sunday, killing all nine aboard. US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the aircraft departed Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas and was headed to the Bahamas before nose-diving near Military Trail and 10th Avenue North and erupting into a fireball that just missed homes. The NTSB is investigating the cause.
items.title: Florida Learjet Crash Kills All Nine Aboard

items.summary: Indian authorities are preparing for Cyclone Murasu, expected to cross the Andhra Pradesh coast near Bapatla on November 3. Chief minister N Chandrababu Naidu directed officials to stay ready for relief operations as heavy to very heavy rain is forecast across parts of three states over the next days. Wind speeds up to 110 kmph are anticipated at landfall, with damage possible to around 15,128 electricity poles across 12 districts. Meanwhile, Odisha continues recovery from Cyclone Arnab, whose death toll rose to six on Sunday as two more bodies were recovered and search continued for 10 missing people.
items.title: Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu brace for Cyclone Murasu

items.summary: Kimi Antonelli became Formula One's youngest world champion, aged 20, after finishing third in the Mexico City Grand Prix. His championship lead reached an unbeatable 119 points. He is also the first Italian driver to win since 1953. The race was stopped by a red flag with 25 of the 71 laps remaining before being restarted; Max Verstappen won and Lewis Hamilton finished second.
items.title: Antonelli Becomes Youngest F1 World Champion at 20

items.summary: Anantapur superintendent of police Jagadeesh told PTI that Hemant, accused of attacking two Class 10 girls with a chainsaw at a government school in Raptadu on October 31, was hiding near the Atmakur forest. Police formed 15 teams and fired around six rounds after he assaulted officers; one inspector was injured. One girl lost her right hand.
items.title: Police Shoot and Nab Chainsaw Attacker in Atmakur Forest

items.summary: Union home minister Amit Shah attacked Congress leader Rahul Gandhi over the INDIA bloc’s ‘Chalo Dilli’ rally at Ramlila Maidan in Delhi, saying if Gandhi wanted to become prime minister he should remain in a “mock parliament” his whole life. Shah said the Congress had lost elections for 15 years and that Sonia Gandhi’s dream of seeing her son as PM remained unfulfilled. He also accused the party of obstructing Parliament over women’s reservation and organising the rally on November 1, linked to the 1984 anti-Sikh riots. The rally came amid a protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
items.title: Amit Shah dismisses Rahul Gandhi as a permanent opposition figure

items.summary: Videos captured a business jet carrying nine people exploding into a fireball near a busy road in Greenacres, Palm Beach County, Florida. US transportation secretary Sean Duffy said all aboard died as cited by AP. Air traffic control recordings show the pilot reporting icing and turbulence before declaring an emergency descent of up to 30,000 feet per minute. The FAA is assisting the NTSB investigation.
items.title: Florida Learjet Crash Kills All Nine Aboard Near Busy Roadway

items.summary: St. Joseph's Church at Perumpannaiyur in Tiruvarur district, built from 1871 and standing about 153 feet tall, is estimated to need Rs 40 crore for a restoration project expected to run roughly three years after beginning in April 2026. The parish has appealed to the public, philanthropists, devotees and government for financial help. Financial strain is compounded by alleged encroachment of church land by a politician, reducing revenue from more than 250 acres it owns.
items.title: Century-old Tamil Nadu church seeks Rs 40 crore restoration after land encroachment

items.summary: EkChitra Art Gallery opened Living Temple II, its second edition celebrating Indian art heritage through over 100 works by more than 30 artists. Founder Annapurna Madipadiga framed the event as a dialogue between ancient knowledge and contemporary expression. Attendee Shilpa Reddy called both editions fortunate experiences, praising Nagendra Babu's 32-foot scroll and an M.S. Subbulakshmi saree collection. The exhibition runs until 29 November 2026.
items.title: Living Temple II Opens at EkChitra Art Gallery

items.summary: Kimi Antonelli became Formula 1's youngest world champion, breaking Sebastian Vettel's record and becoming the first Italian winner since Alberto Ascari in 1953. The 20-year-old Mercedes driver secured the 2026 drivers' title with a third-place finish at Mexico City after four rounds remained. Max Verstappen won ahead of Hamilton, while Antonelli needed only ninth place or better to clinch it. He said he would not be there without Mercedes and his family.
items.title: Antonelli Claims F1 Title as Youngest Ever Champion

items.summary: A month ago, reports claimed oil flows out of Hormuz had recovered to pre-war levels and pushed prices lower, but the rout did not last. Brent benchmarks are set for a fourth monthly gain in a row as Gulf states say they export more than before the war. JP Morgan's Natasha Kaneva told the Wall Street Journal that her model suggests fair value at $94 per barrel of Brent crude, yet it trades above $116. Shipping costs have soared to all-time highs and producing countries discount their oil despite reports about improving flows. UBS strategist Giovanni Staunovo noted a sharp deterioration in maritime security as vessels face attacks and insurance and freight costs rise. The International Energy Agency's Fatih Birol said the disruption will likely continue well into next year, with no credible pathway back to pre-war prices.
items.title: Oil Prices Decouple From Headlines Amid War Premium

items.summary: At the 71st Foundation Day function in Bhopal, Chief Minister Mohan Yadav said Madhya Pradesh was entering a new era of development. He highlighted an industrial growth rate that had reached around 24%, attributing progress to youth, women and farmers. The state ranked third nationally in milk production and received Rs 490 crore in MSME subsidies.
items.title: Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Cites Industrial Growth At Bhopal Foundation Day Event

items.summary: A car salesman in Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh was jailed after being produced before a court on Sunday. Identified as Gajendra alias Rishi Anand, he was arrested by Ashoka Garden police on Saturday following the theft of a luxury car worth Rs 23 lakh from a showroom on September 28. Police say his wife's desire to drive expensive cars motivated him.
items.title: Bhopal Salesman Arrested for Stealing Luxury Car to Fulfil Wife's Wish

items.summary: Villa Vie Residences abruptly ended an indefinite ocean cruise after roughly two years, telling passengers they had less than seven hours notice and to leave by 2 o'clock. Passengers Randy Cassingham and his wife were stranded in Cambodia, the ship's 65th country visited. The company said fuel prices rose three to four times since a war began in Iran; Cassingham disputed that as the full cause, saying the company had been in financial trouble from the start. He paid $379,000 for a cabin with at least 15 years of sailing guaranteed.
items.title: Cruise Ship Ends After Two Years Over Fuel Costs

items.summary: Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary appealed on Sunday to affluent households and income-tax-paying people in the state to voluntarily give up their benefit of 125 units of free electricity, he said. He addressed the two-day Pataliputra National Youth Parliament-2.0 in Patna, saying such contributions would help Bihar's development. Choudhary noted the subsidy costs around Rs 23,000 crore annually and runs at about Rs 8,000-10,000 per household.
items.title: Bihar Chief Minister Urges Wealthy Households and Taxpayers to Surrender Free Power Benefit

items.summary: The Election Commission ordered immediate suspension of Electoral Registration Officers Mayank Goswami and Hemant Chaudhary over alleged irregularities in the 127-Pilibhit Assembly constituency electoral roll. An inquiry found a computer assistant submitted 13,779 Form 8 applications between May 31 and August 29; 10,470 were approved and 3,309 rejected. No application forms or supporting documents were located in the office. The Commission directed chargesheets for scrutiny barring reinstatement without approval, added Section 198 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita to an existing FIR against them and operator Anil Kumar, ordered rigorous case pursuit, verification across constituencies, and termination of the outsourced computer assistant's services.
items.title: Election Commission Suspends Two Pilibhit Poll Officers Over Voter Roll Irregularities

items.summary: Police remained on duty in central Frankfurt on Sunday, 1 November, after riots broke out following a demonstration the previous day. Footage shows smashed shop windows, looted stores and burning barricades across the streets. Several protesters and officers were injured while 30 people were detained. The situation calmed by early morning after police cordoned off parts of the city centre. Violence was also reported in Cologne and Berlin.
items.title: Riots Erupt in Frankfurt After Demonstration, Police Respond With Water Cannon

items.summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi alleged that Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar helped Narendra Modi secure a third term and Amit Shah become home minister, calling the alleged voter-roll deletion “treason” and demanding Kumar’s removal. The rally at Delhi’s Ramlila Maidan drew INDIA bloc leaders and several chief ministers; Mamata Banerjee said her party was made to lose in Bengal, while BJP leader JP Nadda called it a conspiracy to instigate riots. Gandhi accused the BJP of shutting shops near Connaught Place.
items.title: INDIA bloc leaders rally demanding removal of election commissioner over alleged vote theft

items.summary: Hundreds of young demonstrators gathered outside Berlin's Brandenburg Gate on Saturday as part of a nationwide day of youth protests organised by the GenZ regelt! movement. The rally was one of demonstrations planned in more than 30 German cities, including Frankfurt and Cologne, following student protests across several European countries.
items.title: Youth Protesters Gather at Berlin's Brandenburg Gate

items.summary: Protests in France have helped inspire youth demonstrations across Europe, from Portugal and Italy to Germany, according to a report by Charlotte Hughes. In Germany, large Saturday rallies led by an initiative loosely translating as “Gen Z has got this” called for better education and healthcare, stronger climate protection, lower living costs, and opposed reinstating compulsory military service. Demonstrations in several major German cities turned violent late in the day, particularly in Frankfurt.
items.title: Youth-led rallies sweep Europe amid German unrest

items.summary: One week before South Africa's local elections, residents across Johannesburg describe crumbling pavements and roads choked with rubbish, foul-smelling water at the Jukskei River, widespread power cuts and potholes. Semadi Manganye of Alexandra Water Warriors says challenges range from electricity to waste, while Kate Spiller calls the water situation
items.title: Anger mounts over Johannesburg's failing infrastructure ahead of local elections

items.summary: The Central Bureau of Investigation extradited Sourabh Chandrakar, promoter of the Mahadev Online Book app and alleged kingpin of an illegal betting syndicate, from Oman. A special CBI team brought him to India after he was located by the Royal Oman Police following an Interpol Red Corner Notice. He will be produced in Raipur on Monday, undergo a medical examination, and face chargesheets filed under several laws; the CBI described the extradition as significant for bringing transnational fugitives to justice.
items.title: CBI Extradites Mahadev Betting App Promoter From Oman

items.summary: Samajwadi Party leader Mohammad Azam Khan was sent to 14-day jail custody after bail in the dual PAN card case, arrested by the Enforcement Directorate over a money laundering probe linked to Mohammad Ali Jauhar University. The ED told the court he is withholding evidence needed to trace alleged proceeds of crime. On October 28, authorities provisionally attached university land and buildings valued at Rs 426. 46 crore originally and around Rs 1,170 crore now; an assessment put construction cost at Rs 494. 46 crore across 59 buildings, raising total campus valuation to Rs 499. 09 crore against only Rs 78.
items.title: Azam Khan Sent to Custody in Jauhar University Money Laundering Case

items.summary: EL PAÍS USA Edition reports on an InsideHook essay by New York writer Jaed Coffin, who frames declining male hormone levels not as crisis but as grounds for self-acceptance. The piece notes that the average man’s testosterone fell 54% between 1972 and 2019, per a study presented in London at an ESHRE meeting covering around 118,000 men from five countries. It then surveys how public figures — Robert F. Kennedy Jr., J.D. Vance, Scott Galloway, Andrew Tate — have linked masculinity to hormones or politics, and reports the University of Sydney’s analysis that social media is pushing hormone therapy on healthy young men. The article offers no single conclusion beyond describing these competing narratives.
items.title: A Spanish outlet reframes low testosterone as a celebrated identity

items.summary: Since Abdel Fattah al-Sisi took power, Egypt has invested heavily in monumental projects meant to rival ancient achievements and restore the country among leading nations. Cairo now hosts the Grand Egyptian Museum, billed as its largest museum for a single civilization; infrastructure including the 220-foot Tahya Misr bridge certified by Guinness World Records; and the New Administrative Capital with an African-tallest skyscraper and a world-record flagpole since 2021. In July, a new military headquarters called the Octagon was inaugurated, covering 35 square miles and surpassing the Pentagon in size and name. Officials describe these works as embracing tradition while building toward national prominence.
items.title: Egypt pursues pharaonic megaprojects under Sisi's New Republic vision

items.summary: The French Business Cycle Dating Committee (CDCEF) of the French Economic Association (AFSE), led by Laurent Ferrara, released a statement on 10/29/2026 assessing recent French GDP data. The quarterly growth rate for the third quarter of 2026 stands at −0.1%, following a contraction of 0.2% in the first quarter and stagnation in the second. Some commentators argue this sequence implies a technical recession over the first three quarters of 2026, but the CDCEF urges caution, noting GDP figures remain subject to revision and that recessions require evaluating duration, depth and diffusion rather than two negative quarters alone. Cumulative decline since late 2025 is around 0.3%, far below past crises. The committee concludes current data do not support a recession, though sluggish activity warrants monitoring.
items.title: French economic association rules out recession amid near-zero growth

items.summary: CleanTechnica's Zach and Scott modeled two hypothetical Norwegian coastal bulk services to test whether GMI Group's hydrogen-electric ships make economic sense. Over fifteen years, they found hydrogen propulsion 50–58% more expensive than diesel even with roughly €13.1 million in public support assumed upfront, while battery-electric options were cheaper by about €11.64–14.13 million. The results are scenario-based, not GMI's actual contracts; the company has not published route or commercial data needed for a direct assessment.
items.title: Modeler Finds Hydrogen Bulk Carriers Costlier Than Batteries on Two Routes

items.summary: Paul Krugman and Heather Cox Richardson recently posted on Substack, drawing on earlier warnings from GOP media consultant Rick Wilson to argue that Donald Trump may act destructively after losing the midterms. Krugman cites Robert Pape’s ‘gambling for resurrection’ idea, suggesting a politically bankrupt Trump has incentives to provoke upheaval. Richardson points to reports of proposed Putin–Xi talks over Ukraine and quotes Tom Nichols on Trump abandoning Western order, while also noting Andrew McCarthy’s claim that Trump gives aid and comfort to Russia. Both writers frame the situation as an existential threat rooted in what they call political bankruptcy.
items.title: Krugman and Richardson Revive Rick Wilson’s Trump Warning

leads.reason: The lead story on our AI desk.
The same report reached us through two of our feeds.
